title: Fire: Finding Individual Routes for Evacuation Under Flame and Thermal Exposure Constraints
content: Wildfire evacuation routing must account for changing hazards throughout a journey and for thermal exposure accumulated before reaching a destination. This study presents an earliest-arrival vehicle-routing method for directed road networks with legal turns, permitted waiting, destination opening intervals and required stays. The method first searches for a journey that avoids predicted flame contact, then checks its peak heat flux and cumulative thermal exposure across every input scenario. The initial search also provides an arrival-time lower bound, supporting a conditional earliest-arrival certificate when a fully checked journey attains that bound. We evaluated the proposed implementation against a resource-constrained A* reference on 20 designed missions across five Korean regional panels representing four parent wildfire incidents. Two repetitions per implementation produced 80 native macOS executions under a 30-second complete-request deadline. The proposed implementation achieved 100% verified on-time resolution (20/20 missions), comprising 15 checked-route missions and five accepted determinations that no admissible route existed under the specified model. The reference resolved 65% (13/20), all with routes. All 56 returned-route executions passed independent cell-center exposure, flame-contact and trajectory checks. On jointly resolved route executions, arrival times matched, while median computation time was 8.006 seconds for the proposed implementation and 7.344 seconds for the reference. A separate 200-execution constraint ablation on the same missions found that eight travel-only routes encountered predicted flames. Enforcing flame avoidance produced three checked detours arriving 490–531 seconds later and five model-based no-route determinations. Adding peak-flux or cumulative-exposure limits caused no additional route changes on this panel. These findings demonstrate improved completion of checked routing decisions within a fixed computation allowance on the evaluated inputs; independent verification of continuous-road radiation bounds and operational validation remain open.
